title: Returning Client Money and Assets
summary: How to ensure client money, safeguarded funds and client assets, including crypto-assets, can be identified, reconciled and returned promptly in a wind-down or failure.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to ensure client money, safeguarded funds and client assets, including crypto-assets, can be identified, reconciled and returned promptly in a wind-down or failure.
Learning Objectives: Assess the quality of segregation, safeguarding and records for client money and assets
Plan the identification, reconciliation and return of client holdings
Identify shortfall risks and how to prevent them
Syllabus: Client money, safeguarding and custody arrangements across sectors
Reconciliation, books and records and resolution packs
Return mechanics: transfer, distribution and unclaimed balances
Crypto-asset custody: keys, wallets and returning digital assets
Intended Audience: Chief financial officers, chief risk officers and finance and treasury teams at investment firms, payment and e-money institutions, crypto-asset service providers and fund managers
Compliance officers, heads of operations and plan owners responsible for drafting and maintaining recovery and wind-down plans
Executive and non-executive directors who approve the plan and would lead the firm through a crisis
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of finance, risk or compliance in a regulated firm is helpful. No prior experience of recovery or wind-down planning is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Key Attributes of Effective Resolution Regimes for Financial Institutions (2014)
Basel Committee, Principles for Sound Liquidity Risk Management and Supervision (2008)
ISO 22301:2019, Security and Resilience – Business Continuity Management Systems
